basic_info.name: MTS-Dialog and the MEDIQA-Chat 2023 shared tasks
basic_info.description: Two coupled 2023 resources from the same Microsoft-led group that together define the reference evaluation protocol for clinical note generation. MTS-Dialog (Ben Abacha, Yim, Fan, Lin; EACL 2023) is an open collection of 1,701 short doctor-patient conversations paired with the corresponding clinical-note sections and 20 normalised first-level section headers, generated by eight medically trained annotators who wrote simulated conversations from public MTsamples notes across six specialties (General Medicine 1,035, Neurology 296, Orthopedic 208, SOAP 79, Dermatology 56, Allergy/Immunology 27); a 3.6k-pair back-translation-augmented set (French and Spanish) also exists. The MEDIQA-Chat 2023 shared task (ClinicalNLP @ ACL 2023; Ben Abacha, Yim, Adams, Snider, Yetisgen) is the challenge built on top of these corpora: Task A used MTS-Dialog for generating and classifying the summary of a short medical conversation, while Tasks B and C used ACI-BENCH for full clinical-note generation from a full encounter (Task B) and the inverse note-to-dialogue generation (Task C). Its load-bearing fact is that it fixed the official evaluation convention for the field - an aggregate score combining ROUGE-, BERTScore- and BLEURT-family metrics plus human evaluation - and produced the result that still frames expectations: WangLab's GPT-4 in-context-learning system ranked first in Task B, its ROUGE-1 of 0.6141 beat the runner-up by more than nine aggregate points, and in a three-physician human study GPT-4-generated notes were preferred about as often as human-written notes (ICL 50% vs ground-truth 48% win rate excluding ties) while the fine-tuned LED baseline was almost never preferred (2%).
basic_info.organization: Microsoft (Asma Ben Abacha, Wen-wai Yim, Yadan Fan, Thomas Lin; MEDIQA-Chat co-organisers Ben Abacha, Yim, Neal Snider) with University of Washington (Meliha Yetisgen), plus Columbia University (Griffin Adams) as MEDIQA-Chat co-organiser; 120 registered teams and 17 submitting teams from academia and industry
basic_info.country: United States (organisers and datasets); an international field of participating teams including Canada, Singapore, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Croatia and others
basic_info.status: research. The shared task concluded in 2023 and MTS-Dialog has had no dataset version change, but both datasets remain live, widely cited, and used as standard evaluation corpora through 2026 (e.g. CAP at ACL BioNLP 2026, MedHELM 2026, LLaMA-Clinic 2025).

technical_features.what_it_does: MTS-Dialog provides short doctor-patient conversation snippets each paired with a section header and section content from a clinical note, enabling two sub-tasks: (i) generating the summary/section content of a short medical conversation, and (ii) classifying the section using a predefined list of first-level headers (20 normalised types). MEDIQA-Chat 2023 operationalises these plus the inverse at full-encounter scale: Task A is MTS-Dialog summary generation plus header classification; Task B is full-note generation from a full doctor-patient conversation using ACI-BENCH; Task C is note-to-dialogue generation (synthesising a plausible encounter conversation from a clinical note) using ACI-BENCH. The shared task fixes the scoring convention: ROUGE-1/2/L/ROUGE-LSum, BERTScore, BLEURT and an arithmetic-mean Aggregate-Score (average of ROUGE-1, BERTScore and BLEURT) evaluated by an official script, complemented by expert human evaluation of critical omissions, hallucinations and preferences. The MTS-Dialog paper additionally contributes the finding that pre-fine-tuning on XSum beats CNN/DailyMail for this task (ROUGE-1 40.15 vs 32.01) and that guided summarisation raises factual precision but lowers recall. For Module C the load-bearing relevance is that this is the reference protocol - metrics, human-evaluation rubric and omission/hallucination framing - that the Module C evaluation harness should mirror.
technical_features.architecture: A dataset-and-challenge artifact rather than a single model. Data layer: MTS-Dialog (1,701 short dialogue-section pairs, plus 3.6k back-translation pairs) and ACI-BENCH (207 full encounter-note pairs with MEDIQA test splits). Harness layer: the official MEDIQA-Chat evaluation script computing an ensemble of ROUGE (Lin), BERTScore (Zhang) and BLEURT (Sellam), with title/header classification accuracy scored separately. Shared-task methods submitted in 2023 spanned: WangLab's fine-tuned LED (base/large/PubMed) and GPT-4 few-shot in-context learning with similarity-retrieved examples; SummQA's one-shot GPT-4 with dynamic retrieved prompts; Cadence's BART-large fine-tuned on inverse-SamSum plus Task A/B/C data and a two-pass long-input strategy; NUS-IDS T5 fine-tuned with GPT-3-augmented data; HuskyScribe BART-large-xsum plus Clinical-T5-Large; Care4Lang Flan-T5; UMASS_BioNLP's FLAN-BioMedLM and a two-LLM 'doctor-patient loop'; GersteinLab Davinci; iuteam1 LSG-BART; DFKI-MedIML; and ChatGPT/GPT-4 baselines. This is essentially a catalogue of pre-LLM and LLM-era note-generation architectures.
technical_features.inputs: Task A: a short doctor-patient conversation snippet (dialogue text), and for the classification sub-task a predefined list of section headers. Task B: a full encounter transcript, optionally with metadata. Task C: a complete clinical note used as the source to generate a conversation. All text; no audio, images, structured FHIR, vitals or documents are consumed by the task itself (some teams added external data such as MIMIC-IV notes for augmentation).
technical_features.outputs: Task A: a summary/section content plus a predicted section header. Task B: a full clinical note. Task C: a synthetic doctor-patient conversation. Evaluation outputs are numeric: ROUGE-1/2/L/ROUGE-LSum, BERTScore-F1, BLEURT, Aggregate-Score, header-classification accuracy, and for Task C also BLEU, concept recall, and Self-BLEU diversity. No coded document, FHIR resource, Composition or Bundle is produced by any task.
technical_features.standards_compliance: [uncertain] Neither MTS-Dialog nor MEDIQA-Chat conforms to or validates against any clinical document/interoperability standard - there is no FHIR, HL7, Composition, IPS or NRCeS profile, and notes are free-form English clinical prose. The only standardised vocabulary is UMLS, used inside fact/concept-based metrics (UMASS_BioNLP used MedSpaCy to extract UMLS concepts restricted to disease, drug, device and procedure semantic groups and computed concept recall); MTS-Dialog itself uses 20 normalised section headers rather than any standard header ontology, and no SNOMED CT, LOINC or ICD output binding is performed. Any NRCeS OPConsultRecord mapping would be built entirely by MediKiosk.
technical_features.offline_capability: Both datasets and the official evaluation scripts are static and runnable locally once downloaded; there is no server dependency in the benchmark. Task submissions themselves can be produced offline with local models, but the top-performing 2023 entries relied on OpenAI APIs, and MTS-Dialog's original training used 4 NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPUs. There is no sync, encryption or store-and-forward layer because it is a benchmark, not a runtime. For Module C the corpus and metrics can be vendored into an offline India-resident harness.
technical_features.languages_supported: English only for the primary MTS-Dialog and ACI-BENCH data and for all MEDIQA-Chat tasks. A separate MTS-Dialog augmented collection of 3.6k pairs was created via back-translation using French and Spanish, but it is an augmentation artifact, not a multilingual generation capability, and there is no Hindi, Devanagari or Hinglish content.
technical_features.deployment_model: A downloadable research dataset plus shared-task/evaluation infrastructure intended for local, laptop or cluster use. There is no kiosk, clinic-LAN, room-server or cloud deployment model. MTS-Dialog's original model baselines were trained on 4 NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPUs, and later entrants used API-served models; the data and metric harness themselves are small enough to run on modest hardware.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: MEDIQA-Chat 2023 Task A (MTS-Dialog): WangLab's jointly header-and-content Flan-T5 model achieved the best summarization subtask Aggregate-Score of 0.5789 and tied for best header classification accuracy of 0.78; run scores included ROUGE-1 0.4466, ROUGE-2 0.2282, ROUGE-L/LSum 0.3837, BERTScore 0.7307, BLEURT 0.5593. SummQA (one-shot GPT-4) reached Aggregate-Score 0.5753; NUS-IDS 0.5204; baselines were ChatGPT 0.4887 and GPT-4 0.4949. UMASS_BioNLP reported FLAN-BioMedLM header accuracy 0.705 versus ChatGPT 0.355. Task B (ACI-BENCH full note): WangLab's GPT-4 ICL achieved the best ROUGE-1 of 0.6141 and section-based Aggregate-Score of 0.6483, beating the runner-up by more than nine aggregate points; SummQA reached 0.5541; the official GPT-4 baseline scored ROUGE-1 0.5176 and the ChatGPT baseline 0.4887. Human evaluation with three senior resident physicians on 20 validation examples: win rate excluding ties was Ground Truth 48%, GPT-4 ICL 50%, fine-tuned LED 2% (raw preferences GT 23 / ICL 24 / FT 1, with 10 ties and 2 FT-ICL ties), i.e. GPT-4 notes were preferred about as often as human notes and strongly preferred over the fine-tuned model, though inter-annotator agreement was low. Task C (note-to-dialogue): Cadence's BART-large had the best ROUGE-1 of 0.5435; UMASS_BioNLP's doctor-patient loop reported concept recall 47.19 short and 51.23 long with Self-BLEU 0.013 short; GPT-4-short reached ROUGE-1 53.16 and concept recall 44.95. MTS-Dialog's own paper reported that XSum pre-fine-tuning beats CNN/DailyMail (ROUGE-1 40.15 vs 32.01) and, in expert manual evaluation, best-model summary fluency 2.44 on a 0-3 scale with factual F1 0.76, but a 3% hallucination rate and 33% of medical facts missed; data augmentation improved fluency/recall but raised hallucination from 1% to 3%, while guided summarisation improved fact precision by 5.5% and lowered recall by 5%.
performance_metrics.latency: [uncertain] No latency, throughput or time-to-summary figures are reported for the datasets or for the 2023 baselines. The only compute context given is hardware used for training (MTS-Dialog baselines on 4 NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPUs over 4 epochs) and the API-based inference for GPT-4 entries; the shared task was not scored on speed. Latency must therefore be measured independently by Module C on its own hardware.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Data is small: MTS-Dialog is 1,701 short pairs (15,969 dialogue turns / 241,685 words; 5,870 summary sentences / 81,299 words) plus a 3.6k augmented set; ACI-BENCH is 207 full pairs. Running the official metric suite requires Python plus transformer models for BERTScore and BLEURT, and fact/concept metrics may need MedSpaCy/UMLS resources. Training the 2023 baselines needed multi-GPU (e.g. 4x Tesla K80 for MTS-Dialog models; LED-Large is ~460M parameters, FLAN-T5-Large ~780M, BART-large ~400M). No kiosk-class runtime exists; the metric harness itself is far lighter than any of these models.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: MTS-Dialog: 1,701 pairs total (TRAIN 1,201, VALIDATION 100, TEST1 200 MEDIQA-Chat Task A, TEST2 200 MEDIQA-SUM 2023 Task A/B) plus 3.6k back-translation-augmented pairs; 279 original headers normalised to 20 first-level types; 8 medically trained annotators; ~1,800 cumulative annotator hours; specialty mix General Medicine 1,035, Neurology 296, Orthopedic 208, SOAP 79, Dermatology 56, Allergy/Immunology 27. ACI-BENCH: 207 pairs (67/20/40/40/40). MEDIQA-Chat 2023: 120 registered teams, 17 teams submitted code and runs, with 14 in Task A, 9 in Task B, and a smaller set in Task C. Repository metrics: MTS-Dialog GitHub 129 stars / 22 forks / 3 open issues; ACI-BENCH 83 stars / 5 forks.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Peer-reviewed throughout: MTS-Dialog at EACL 2023 (pp. 2291-2302) and the MEDIQA-Chat 2023 overview at the ClinicalNLP workshop at ACL 2023. MTS-Dialog's study evaluates multiple SOTA summarisation models with n-gram (ROUGE), embedding (BERTScore, including the deberta-xlarge-mnli variant best correlated with humans), learned (BLEURT-20), and fact-based (Fact Scores) metrics, then grounds them with an expert manual evaluation using NLG criteria (fluency, non-redundancy) and medical criteria (critical omissions, hallucinations), and studies automatic-human metric correlation; inter-annotator fact-F1 agreement was 0.875 (exact) / 0.957 (relaxed) with fact-count Pearson correlation 0.862. MEDIQA-Chat 2023 used a fixed official evaluation script with the ensemble metrics, capped submissions at three runs per task, and included expert human comparison for the leading systems; the WangLab human study used three senior residents on 20 validation examples with notes presented in random order as A/B/C. Follow-up reuse in 2025-2026 (LLaMA-Clinic blinded physician reader study; CAP GPT-5.1 judge on a 197-case ACI-Bench cohort; MedHELM Q2 2026 jury scoring) shows the protocol has been extended with LLM judges and rubric scoring, but the original automatic metrics remain the comparability anchor.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: This pair supplies the exact evaluation harness template Module C needs. First, MEDIQA-Chat's metric suite - ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT and an aggregate - is the accepted way to report dialogue-to-note fidelity, so Module C can adopt it verbatim (locally) and be directly comparable to published numbers. Second, the human-evaluation design is the template for Module C's physician-attestation validation: blinded side-by-side preference against ground truth plus explicit critical-omission and hallucination counting, which the MTS-Dialog study showed is essential because automatic metrics do not track factual consistency. Third, the headline finding that GPT-4 ICL notes were preferred about as often as human notes while a fine-tuned LED was almost never preferred is the strongest available evidence for the 'LLM as renderer, deterministic slots as truth' split, and equally the strongest warning that a generic cloud LLM is a credible competitor on raw note quality - which is why MediKiosk must differentiate on provenance, conformance and offline operation rather than on winning a preference test. Fourth, the MTS-Dialog finding that the best 2023 models still missed 33% of medical facts and hallucinated at 3% is direct quantitative justification for Module C's omission and hallucination gates. Fifth, Task A's section-header classification sub-task maps onto Module C's problem of routing elicited history into the correct OPConsultRecord sections and gives a precedent for scoring that routing as accuracy.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) the official ensemble metric definition (arithmetic mean of ROUGE-1, BERTScore and BLEURT, reported alongside per-metric values) so Module C's numbers are comparable to the 2023 leaderboard; (b) the explicit critical-omission / hallucination / preference human-evaluation rubric, adapted to physician attestation of an OPConsultRecord summary; (c) concept recall in the UMASS_BioNLP sense (UMLS restricted to disease, drug, device, procedure) as a third fidelity axis, re-bound to SNOMED CT India / CDCI / NAMASTE because UMLS licensing is unsuitable for an Indian product; (d) section-header classification accuracy as the metric for correct section routing; (e) MTS-Dialog's recognition that summarisation must be scored for factual consistency against the source, not just n-gram overlap; (f) reporting of Self-BLEU/diversity for any synthetic-data generation lane. Adapt: build an Indic, code-mixed and AYUSH-aware counterpart corpus because MTS-Dialog and ACI-BENCH are US English. Reject: the reliance on GPT-4 API ICL and any cloud judge as the production path - it conflicts with offline and India-residency constraints; and reject using a single preference win as proof of safety, since the same study showed low inter-annotator agreement and large unmeasured omission rates.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Both corpora are synthetic and US-English. MTS-Dialog conversations were invented by annotators from MTsamples notes rather than captured from real encounters, and its summaries are section extracts, so it models snippet-level generation rather than full-encounter note writing. ACI-BENCH is role-play with machine-drafted then human-edited notes. The headline evidence is small and noisy: the WangLab human study involved only three physicians on 20 cases, inter-annotator agreement was explicitly low, and the win-rate difference between GPT-4 and ground truth (50% vs 48%) is within noise, so it should not be read as a stable ranking. The MTS-Dialog manual evaluation found the best model hallucinated 3% of the time and omitted 33% of facts, and that augmentation traded hallucination rate against recall - a reminder that high automatic scores coexist with material factual gaps. The MEDIQA-Chat results are a snapshot of the GPT-4/ChatGPT era; the task stopped in 2023, so leaderboard numbers are historical and not a current SOTA claim. Metric limitations persist: ROUGE penalises paraphrase and misses entailment, and the MTS-Dialog paper itself notes poor correlation between automatic and human judgement. There is no standard conformance or coding evaluation at all, no offline/privacy evaluation, and no Indic or AYUSH dimension, so the benchmark cannot certify any of MediKiosk's differentiators.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: This is a benchmark-and-protocol artifact, not a competing system, so it erodes none of MediKiosk's differentiators and can be adopted wholesale as evaluation infrastructure. It differs from MediKiosk in that it is US-English, synthetic, text-only, cloud-model-centric in its best-performing entries, has no runtime, no encryption/sync, no FHIR/NRCeS/ABDM emission, no physician-attestation artifact and no AYUSH history model - it measures only the fidelity of generated note text. It strengthens MediKiosk by providing a defensible, peer-reviewed and directly comparable fidelity protocol (ROUGE + BERTScore + BLEURT aggregate, concept recall, header accuracy, plus blinded human preference with omission/hallucination counting) and by quantifying the exact risks - 33% of facts omitted, 3% hallucinated - that Module C's per-field provenance, elicit-never-diagnose posture and physician attestation are designed to contain. The correct framing is that MEDIQA-Chat supplies the measurement apparatus while leaving MediKiosk's offline, India-residency, NRCeS-conformant-emission and attestation claims entirely unmeasured by prior art.

business_info.license: MTS-Dialog and its data are published under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), explicitly stated in the repository README. ACI-BENCH (the Tasks B/C corpus) is likewise CC BY 4.0. The MEDIQA-Chat 2023 shared-task repository and evaluation code carry no explicit standalone LICENSE file [uncertain - no license file was found on the task repository, so code-reuse terms should be confirmed with the organisers even though the data is CC BY].
business_info.pricing: Free. Both datasets and the shared-task evaluation code are openly downloadable with no pricing, subscription or commercial tier; access is limited only by the requirement to cite the associated papers (and, for anything reusing UMLS-based concept metrics, respecting UMLS licensing).
business_info.funding: No venture funding; corporate and academic research output from Microsoft (with University of Washington and Columbia co-authors) plus a 3.6k-pair augmentation created with Microsoft annotators. The shared task ran as an academic workshop challenge at ClinicalNLP @ ACL 2023 and CLEF ImageCLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 with broader academic participation, but no disclosed grant or round.
business_info.commercial_status: Unpaid open research resource. Neither MTS-Dialog nor MEDIQA-Chat is a commercial product or service; they are academic datasets and a one-off shared task, freely used by researchers and, indirectly, by commercial vendors benchmarking against them.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Within the clinical note-generation evaluation space: MTS-Dialog competes with ACI-BENCH (full encounters, same authors), primock57 (57 real full encounters), the 3M Health, Abridge, Augmedix, emr.ai and Nuance private corpora that dominate by volume but are closed, plus later evaluation efforts such as DischargeMe and the MedHELM healthcare benchmark suite which now packages ACI-Bench. The MEDIQA-Chat shared task itself was mirrored by CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 (same datasets, Tasks A-C on MTS-Dialog and ACI-BENCH). None overlaps the offline + ABDM + pre-consultation-summary space.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: No clinical-system integrations (no EHR/HIS, ABDM HIP/HIU/PHR, health locker or messaging). Its integrations are research-tooling: the datasets are aggregated in Microsoft's clinical_visit_note_summarization_corpus, the official evaluation script is a reusable artifact, ACI-BENCH is embedded in MedHELM's runnable suite and EnvCommons/ACIBench, and the protocol is reused by 2025-2026 model papers (LLaMA-Clinic, CAP). Module C can vendor the datasets and metric script offline but there is no live integration.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The 2023 shared task was the inflection point where the field moved from fine-tuned encoder-decoders to LLM few-shot generation, and the ecosystem has since shifted again toward LLM-judge and rubric-based evaluation (MedHELM Q2 2026 jury scores, EnvCommons/ACIBench rubric grading by gpt-5-mini, CAP's GPT-5.1 judge). This is a tailwind because Module C can cheaply build a rubric harness, and a caution because the industry default is now a cloud LLM judge, which clashes with the kiosk's offline and India-residency constraints - so Module C should implement judge-style scoring with a small local model or a deterministic rubric. The persistent ecosystem gap is that no benchmark in this family evaluates FHIR/ABDM conformance, Indic languages, code-mixed Hinglish or AYUSH history, leaving MediKiosk able to claim a measurement category the mainstream benchmark world has not yet built.

history.release_date: MTS-Dialog first released 2023-01-27 (GitHub repository created) and published at EACL 2023 (2023-05-03 to 2023-05-05, Dubrovnik). The MEDIQA-Chat 2023 shared task ran under ClinicalNLP @ ACL 2023, with its overview paper published in the workshop proceedings (2023); the companion CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 ran separately.
history.key_milestones: 2023-01-27: MTS-Dialog GitHub repository created. 2023-05: MTS-Dialog presented at EACL 2023 and the EACL paper published. 2023: MEDIQA-Chat 2023 shared task at ClinicalNLP @ ACL 2023 - 120 registered teams, 17 submitting; Task A on MTS-Dialog and Tasks B/C on ACI-BENCH. 2023: WangLab's GPT-4 ICL ranked first in Task B and its human study reported GPT-4 notes preferred about as often as human notes. 2023: CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 mirrored the tasks. 2023-06/09: ACI-BENCH (the Tasks B/C corpus) released as preprint and in Nature Scientific Data. 2025: LLaMA-Clinic (ACL Findings 2025) reused these datasets for a blinded physician reader study (92.8% acceptable-or-higher). 2026: CAP (ACL BioNLP 2026) reuses ACI-Bench with a GPT-5.1 judge and source-grounded proposition metrics; MedHELM Q2 2026 retains ACI-Bench as a clinical documentation scenario; EnvCommons/ACIBench packages it as an agent environment.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: No new release or dataset update occurred for MTS-Dialog, ACI-BENCH, or the MEDIQA-Chat task itself in the last six months; they are stable, closed 2023 artifacts. Activity in the window is downstream reuse and re-packaging of the same corpora and protocol: CAP appeared at ACL BioNLP 2026 (within the window) proposing Clinical Atomic Propositions and evaluating five methods on a filtered 197-case ACI-Bench cohort with a GPT-5.1 judge and source-grounded semCAP recall/precision/F1 (CAP improved semCAP-R from 0.574 to 0.694 over transcript-only); MedHELM's Q2 2026 (v0.7) leaderboard, maintained with Stanford CRFM, retained ACI-Bench as a clinical documentation generation scenario (top jury score 4.969); and EnvCommons/ACIBench continued to offer a rubric-scored single-turn agent version of the corpus (114/35/210 splits graded by gpt-5-mini). The environment's real movement is the migration of evaluation from the ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT ensemble toward LLM-judge and rubric scoring - a protocol change Module C must account for while keeping the 2023 ensemble metrics for comparability.

market_positioning.target_users: Clinical NLP and medical-LLM researchers, shared-task participants and model developers; secondarily healthcare AI evaluation teams and vendors needing a public, citable benchmark. Not built for patients, clinicians in the loop, hospitals or governments, though governance teams may reference it.
market_positioning.market_segment: Benchmarking and evaluation methodology for clinical note generation - the measurement and reproducibility layer of ambient clinical documentation, adjacent to but distinct from ambient scribing products, intake platforms, PHR and FHIR tooling.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: MTS-Dialog positions itself as the first openly released dataset of doctor-patient conversations with clinical notes and the first study to pair it with detailed automated and manual evaluation of clinical note generation, aimed at reducing a documentation burden estimated at 52-102 minutes of physician note-writing per day; it sells itself as the resource that unblocks wider NLP research on medical note generation. MEDIQA-Chat 2023 positions itself as the shared task that brings together practitioner and academic teams to define and compare methods for summarising and generating doctor-patient conversations, using ensemble metrics chosen because they correlate well with human judgements, and it frames the release of GPT-4/ChatGPT-era results as a way to develop and understand state-of-the-art approaches for this domain-specific text-generation problem.
